sc-1.title: AI 101: What Is AI and Why Should I Care?

slides.title: AI 101
slides.subtitle: What Is AI and Why Should I Care?

slides.title: What We'll Cover Today
items: What AI actually is, in plain language
AI you already use every day
A live ChatGPT demo, hands-on
What AI can't do (and shouldn't)
Your questions, our answers

slides.title: AI Is Not What You Think
bullets: AI is software that learns from examples
It is not a robot, not a brain, not magic
It guesses the next best word, image, or answer
Like autocomplete, but a million times bigger
Built by people. Owned by companies. Used by you.
slides.note: Frame this as removing mystery, not adding fear. The goal is comfort with the term.

slides.title: Three Words to Know
bullets: Algorithm — a recipe a computer follows
Model — the trained system that makes the guesses
Prompt — what you type to ask the AI for help
That's it. That's the whole vocabulary for today.

slides.title: You're Already an AI User
bullets: Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant — speech AI
Netflix recommendations — pattern AI
Google Maps traffic predictions — prediction AI
Spam filters in your email — sorting AI
Photo tagging on your phone — image AI
slides.note: Pause here and ask the room which ones surprise them. Most people don't realize how many they already use.

slides.text: Most South Carolinians have used AI a hundred times this week. They just didn't know what to call it.

slides.title: Try It Yourself: First Prompt
steps: Open chat.openai.com on your phone or laptop
Type: 'Explain how a thunderstorm works to a 10-year-old in Columbia, SC'
Read the answer out loud with your neighbor
Now try: 'Write a thank-you note to my grandmother for the peach cobbler'
Notice how it changes when you change the question

slides.title: What Just Happened
bullets: You asked a question in plain English
The AI gave a real, useful answer in seconds
You did not need to know any code
You did not need a computer science degree
You can do this every day, for free, starting now

slides.title: AI Has Real Limits
bullets: It can be confidently wrong — always double-check facts
It does not know about events after its training cutoff
It does not understand you the way a friend does
It cannot replace your judgment, your values, or your relationships
It is a tool. You are still the boss.
slides.note: This slide is the most important. Plant the flag: AI helps; humans decide.

slides.title: When NOT to Trust AI
bullets: Medical decisions — talk to a doctor
Legal questions with real stakes — talk to a lawyer
Anything that asks for your bank info or password
Anything that sounds 'too good to be true'
Anything where being wrong would really hurt you

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: A plain-language definition of what AI is
Three vocabulary words that unlock the rest
Hands-on experience using ChatGPT for a real task
A clear sense of what AI is good and bad at
An invitation back: every SCAiL workshop is free

sc-2.title: AI for Your Job: Practical Skills Workshop

slides.title: What We'll Cover Today
items: AI tools that fit your specific job
Building a stronger resume with AI
Writing better emails in less time
Finding job opportunities you'd miss otherwise
Hands-on practice with real workplace tasks

slides.title: Module 1: AI for Your Specific Job
There's an AI for That
bullets: Admin and office work — drafting, scheduling, summarizing
Healthcare — note-taking, patient communication, scheduling
Agriculture — weather, crop monitoring, equipment alerts
Retail and service — inventory, customer messages, training
Skilled trades — quotes, scheduling, supplier research
slides.note: Ask the room what they do for work and pick 2-3 to demo live.

slides.text: The biggest AI gap in South Carolina isn't between people and machines. It's between people who use AI for an hour a week and people who never opened it.

slides.title: Your Resume, Sharper
bullets: Paste your current resume into ChatGPT
Ask: 'How would you improve this for a [job title] role?'
Ask: 'Rewrite my work history using stronger action verbs'
Ask: 'Tailor this to a job description I'll paste below'
You stay in charge — accept what helps, reject what doesn't

slides.title: Hands-On: Resume Tune-Up
steps: Open ChatGPT or Google Gemini on the laptop in front of you
Type or paste 3-5 lines of your work history
Ask the AI to rewrite them with stronger action verbs
Compare the original and the new version side by side
Pick the changes you actually like — keep your voice

slides.title: Faster, Clearer, Less Stressful
bullets: Ask AI to draft a first version, then edit by hand
Use it to soften a frustrated email before you send it
Use it to translate a confusing email into plain English
Use it to write a follow-up when you're stuck on what to say
Always read it before you send. Always.

slides.title: Hands-On: Email Rewrite
steps: Think of an email you've been putting off
Type the situation in plain English to ChatGPT
Ask: 'Help me write a polite, professional email about this'
Read what it gives you out loud
Edit until it sounds like you, then save it as a draft

slides.title: Hidden Doors
bullets: Ask AI: 'What jobs in [your county] match my background?'
Use AI to write a strong LinkedIn About section
Use AI to prepare for interview questions
Use AI to research a company before you apply
Use AI to draft thank-you notes after interviews

slides.title: Hands-On: Pick One Real Task
steps: Pick one workplace task you do every week
Open ChatGPT and describe the task in your own words
Ask the AI to help you do it faster or better
Try the result, then refine your prompt
Save the prompt. You'll use it again.

slides.title: What to Do Tomorrow
bullets: Bookmark ChatGPT or Gemini on your phone
Pick one daily task to try AI on this week
Tell a coworker what you learned today
Come back to SCAiL for the next workshop
Ask us anything by email — we read every message

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: A working AI tool you can use Monday morning
A sharper resume built in front of you today
A draft email that used to take you an hour
A clearer job search strategy
Confidence that AI is a tool you can use, not fear

slides.title: Four Weeks, Four Wins
items: Week 1: AI for marketing — social, ads, content
Week 2: AI for operations — inventory, scheduling, admin
Week 3: AI for customer service — chatbots, email, reviews
Week 4: Building your own AI strategy

slides.text: If you can describe your business in plain English to another person, you can use AI in your business today. That's the whole bar.

slides.title: Marketing on a Tight Budget
bullets: Generate a week of social posts in 20 minutes
Write product descriptions that actually sound human
Draft Facebook and Instagram ads that convert
Translate your marketing into Spanish or other languages
Create images for your menu, store, or service list
slides.note: This is usually the moment a small business owner sees the value. Spend extra time here.

slides.title: Hands-On: Your First AI Social Post
steps: Tell ChatGPT what your business does in 2 sentences
Ask: 'Write 5 Instagram captions for my business this week'
Pick the one that sounds most like you
Ask: 'Make this one shorter and punchier'
Save it for next week's posting schedule

slides.title: The Boring Stuff, Faster
bullets: Inventory tracking with AI photo recognition
Schedule planning with conflict detection
Receipt and expense sorting with AI scanning
Vendor and supplier research in minutes, not hours
Meeting notes auto-summarized and emailed to your team

slides.title: Tools to Try This Week
bullets: ChatGPT and Gemini — general assistants
Notion AI — notes, plans, and project tracking
Otter.ai — meeting transcripts and summaries
Canva — AI-assisted design for free
Google Workspace + Gemini — built into your existing tools

slides.title: Better Service, Less Burnout
bullets: Auto-respond to common questions with a chatbot
Draft replies to negative reviews calmly and professionally
Send personalized thank-you notes at scale
Translate customer messages in real time
Spot patterns in customer feedback you'd otherwise miss

slides.title: Hands-On: Hard Customer Email
steps: Think of a hard customer interaction you had recently
Describe it neutrally to ChatGPT
Ask: 'Help me write a calm, professional response'
Edit it to sound like you
Use this approach next time you're frustrated

slides.title: Pick Your Wins
bullets: Where do you waste the most time each week?
Where do you lose the most money to inefficiency?
What part of your business do you dread the most?
Pick ONE — that's your first AI project
Master one tool before adding a second

slides.title: Your AI Adoption Plan
bullets: Pick 2 tools to use weekly for the next 30 days
Track time saved — write it down
Tell one other business owner what worked
Reassess at day 30 — keep what works, drop what doesn't
Come back to SCAiL for advanced workshops

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: Two AI tools you'll use this month
A 4-week implementation plan that fits your business
Real time saved on marketing, ops, and service
A clearer view of where AI fits — and where it doesn't
A SCAiL community that has your back

slides.title: AI for Farmers
slides.subtitle: Practical Tools for South Carolina Agriculture

slides.title: What We'll Cover Today
items: AI in precision agriculture
Weather prediction tools
Crop monitoring with AI
Livestock management tools
Finding grants and subsidies with AI
Hands-on demos you can take home

slides.text: South Carolina farmers have always used the best tools they could get their hands on. AI is the next tool. Same job, sharper edge.

slides.title: What Precision Ag Actually Means
bullets: Knowing exactly what your land needs, where, and when
Less wasted seed, fertilizer, water, and time
Sensors and satellites doing the watching for you
Decisions based on real data, not just gut
Already in use across SC peach and row crop operations
slides.note: Many farmers think this is for big corporate farms only. It is not.

slides.title: Tools That Pay for Themselves
bullets: Climate FieldView — field-by-field crop tracking
Granular — farm management with AI insights
John Deere Operations Center — equipment + AI integration
FarmLogs — free for small operations
Most have free trials and SC dealer support

slides.title: Smarter Than the Local Forecast
bullets: Hyperlocal weather AI down to the field level
Frost warnings 48-72 hours out for sensitive crops
Storm tracking that helps you plan irrigation and harvest
Drought outlooks that help you plan for the season
Free tools: Windy.com, ClimaCell, NOAA AI feeds

slides.title: Eyes in the Sky
bullets: Drones with AI imaging spot disease before you can
Satellite AI flags moisture stress across acres
Pest detection from photos on your phone
Yield predictions weeks before harvest
Many tools are free or USDA-subsidized

slides.title: AI for Animals
bullets: Smart collars and ear tags track health and location
AI alerts you when an animal is sick or in distress
Feed optimization based on individual animal data
Calving and lambing alerts straight to your phone
Less time chasing problems, more time fixing them

slides.title: AI as Your Grant Researcher
bullets: Ask ChatGPT: 'What USDA grants apply to a small SC peach farm?'
Use AI to draft your first grant application
Find SC-specific cost-share programs you didn't know existed
Research crop insurance options in plain English
Save hours on paperwork you used to dread

slides.title: Hands-On: Find a Grant
steps: Open ChatGPT on the laptop or tablet provided
Type your county and main crop or livestock
Ask: 'What federal and state ag grants apply to me?'
Read the list out loud — circle the 2 most relevant
Take the list home and call your county extension office

slides.title: What You Saw Today
bullets: Real AI tools running on real SC farm data
Free and low-cost options for every farm size
USDA and Clemson Extension partnerships available
Local dealers who can help you set things up
A SCAiL contact who'll answer questions later

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: At least one AI tool you'll try on your operation
A grant or subsidy lead worth pursuing
Plain-English understanding of precision ag
Names of SC ag extension contacts who can help
An invitation to the next SCAiL ag workshop
